gloss: Oda Nobunaga (1534-1582), warlord and first great unifier of Japan

definitions.gloss: Oda Nobunaga, warlord who began the unification of Japan
definitions.explanation: A powerful daimyo of the {戦国|せんごく} (Warring States) period who broke the old feudal order and began unifying Japan by force, only to be betrayed and killed by one of his own generals at {本能寺|ほんのうじ}. He is the archetype of the ruthless, innovative reformer in popular history and fiction.

examples.english: Nobunaga was betrayed by one of his own retainers at the Incident at Honnoji and took his own life.

notes:
{織田信長|おだのぶなが} was the first of the three great unifiers of Japan, followed by his general ⟦{豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし}→豊臣秀吉：30993_toyotomihideyoshi⟧ and then {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}. He is remembered as a ruthless, innovative reformer who broke with tradition — adopting European firearms early and attacking rival Buddhist institutions — and his sudden death remains one of the most famous betrayals in Japanese history.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- {本能寺|ほんのうじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{変|へん}→変：01124_hen⟧: the Incident at Honnoji (1582), where his general {明智光秀|あけちみつひで} forced him to suicide — a byword for sudden betrayal.
- A well-known saying attributed to him and his successors, "if the cuckoo won't sing, kill it" (Nobunaga's line, contrasted with Hideyoshi's "make it want to sing" and Ieyasu's "wait for it to sing"), is used to characterize the three unifiers' different temperaments.
- He appears constantly in period dramas, novels, and video games as the archetypal bold, ruthless reformer.
